newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks seen firmer, but upside limited.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks seen firmer, but upside limited.

text.p: The Tokyo stock market is likely to maintain a firm tone on Wednesday with the high-technology sector continuing to attract investors, brokers said.
But they said the key market index is not likely to extend its recent gains by much due to profit-taking pressure.

On Tuesday, the 225-share Nikkei average finished the session at 20,563.16, up 111.31 points, or 0.54 percent. It was its highest close since 20,568.38 on December 11. Nikkei 225 June futures closed at 20,560, up 120 points.
"I don't expect the Nikkei 225 to post a sharp rally," said a broker at a second-tier Japanese securities house.
Brokers said investors would remain interested in high-tech firms with solid earnings, such as Sony Corp and Fujitsu Ltd.
But they added that the key Nikkei index was not expected to break through above 20,600 easily, as heavy profit taking was likely in that zone.
In other indices, the TOPIX index also rose modestly by 3.39 points or 0.22 percent to 1,515.32, and the Nikkei 300 edged up 0.72 point or 0.25 percent to 292.63.
Among laggards in the high-technology sector, Kyocera jumped sharply.
The ceramic package maker surge 540 yen to 9,050 by midday, a new high for this calendar year, making it the fourth-biggest percentage gainer on the first section.
On the over-the-counter (OTC) market, I-O Data Device Inc , a manufacturer of personal computer peripheral equipment, also advanced to a new 1997 high.
